title: No inertia/momentum when scrolling to change month
line: A quick touchpad swipe in the calendar now moves to the previous or next month instead of snapping back.
explanation: Touchpad scrolling reaches the calendar's page list as wheel events with pixel deltas, which Flickable turns into a drag that follows the fingers. When the fingers lift, the drag never becomes a flick, so the list just snaps to the nearest page and the month only changes if the swipe went past half a page. The list now notes when it is being dragged by wheel events and, if such a drag ends more than a sixth of a page away from the current page, flicks on to that page, like a touchscreen swipe does. This covers the month, year and decade pages.

commits.message:
components/calendar: Finish short touchpad swipes on the next page

Touchpads move the calendar with wheel events that drag it but never
flick it, so a quick swipe snapped back unless it passed half a page.
Flick to the next page when such a swipe ends past a sixth of a page.

BUG: 528586

media.caption: Master: a 150 px touchpad swipe down moves the page (middle), then it snaps back to November
Fixed: the same swipe goes on to October
Master: 150 px swipe towards the previous month snaps back
Fixed: the same swipe changes to October
Master: 150 px swipe towards the next month snaps back
Fixed: the same swipe changes to December

reviews.text: Handling touchpad scroll-phase drags in InfiniteList.qml is the right layer to work around Flickable not turning Wayland touchpad wheel drags into flicks, and the harness tests show the basic swipe case works. However, the wheelDragging state can leak across non-vertical scrolls, onDragEnded ignores dragHandled so long drags can double-advance, and the distance-only height/6 check does not account for swipe direction or velocity.
changes: Prevent wheelDragging from leaking on horizontal or non-dragging wheel events: only set wheelDragging when wheel.pixelDelta.y !== 0 (or draggingVertically is active) and clear it on non-wheel onDragStarted so a later touch or mouse drag cannot falsely enter the wheel-drag flick path.

Check dragHandled in onDragEnded before scheduling flick(): if a single touchpad drag already crossed a full page (setting dragHandled = true and resetting contentY to height) and continued more than height/6 before lifting, Qt.callLater(flick, ...) currently runs after onDraggingVerticallyChanged resets dragHandled and skips a second month.

Factor in swipe direction/velocity rather than only final displacement > height/6 (at minimum verify the last wheel delta direction matches offset and skip the manual flick when already past height/2 where ListView's own snap takes over), so pulling back to cancel a slow drag snaps back instead of rocketing forward at maximumFlickVelocity.

reviews.text: Correct diagnosis: touchpad wheel events become a Flickable drag that never turns into a flick, so StrictlyEnforceRange/SnapToItem snaps back unless the drag passed half a page. Flicking on to the neighbouring page when a wheel-driven drag ends past a sixth of a page gives the page-swipe behaviour the reporter asked for, reuses the existing atYBeginning/atYEnd date-change path (so it changes exactly one month/year/decade), and leaves mouse wheels and touchscreen drags alone. The flick direction is right and the harness reproduces QtWayland's real touchpad event sequence; before/after media match the captions. Nitpicks only: the trigger is distance-based rather than velocity-based (a slow 1/6 drag also flips), and wheelDragging is only cleared in onDragEnded, so a ScrollUpdate that never starts a drag could leave it set for a later touch drag; clearing it when draggingVertically goes false would be more robust.
